mainTopic: Miracle stories of poor צדיקים (רבי חנינא בן דוסא, רבי אלעזר בן פדת) and stories of sages bringing rain
overview: This amud tells a chain of stories about poor צדיקים and about praying for rain. First, a miracle fills the empty oven of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's wife with bread, and a golden table leg is given from Heaven and then taken back so their reward in עולם הבא stays whole. More miracles of רבי חנינא בן דוסא follow: a vinegar lamp burns all שבת, his goats bring home bears, and a neighbor's short beams grow, as פלימו testifies. The גמרא asks how a poor man could own goats, and רב פנחס explains that they came from someone else's lost chickens. Next, the poor רבי אלעזר בן פדת dreams that ה׳ offers to restart the world; he declines and is promised great reward in עולם הבא. The גמרא then returns to fasting for rain: רבי חמא בר חנינא brings rain by rebuking the sky, and לוי brings rain with harsh words but becomes lame. רבי חייא בר לוליני pleads that the rain should fall on ישראל and not on the nations. Finally he begins explaining why a צדיק is compared to both a palm tree and a cedar, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The evil neighbor suspects the empty oven
steps.stepSummary: The wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא lights her oven out of embarrassment. A wicked neighbor knows they have nothing, so she knocks on the door to expose her. The wife hides in an inner room in shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: She did this because of embarrassment. She had a certain evil neighbor, who said: 'I know they have nothing at all, so what is all this smoke?' She went and knocked on the door. The wife was embarrassed and went into an inner room.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from the previous lines. The wife heats an empty oven so the neighbors won't see her poverty, and a mean neighbor comes to catch her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening words explain why she lit the oven: to avoid the shame of being seen with no bread for שבת. The neighbor knows the family is poor, so the smoke makes her suspicious. This sets up the problem that the miracle will solve.
steps.confusionAlert: The words מִשּׁוּם כִּיסּוּפָא finish a sentence earlier: she lit the oven every ערב שבת because of embarrassment. They are not a new statement on their own.

phrases.english: because of embarrassment.
phrases.notes: Finishes the previous sentence: she lit the empty oven so people would think she was baking.

phrases.english: She had a certain evil neighbor,
who said: Now, I know
that they have nothing at all,
so what is all this?
phrases.notes: What is all this smoke coming from the oven?

phrases.english: She went and knocked on the door,
she (the wife) was embarrassed and went into an inner room,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לַהּ הָךְ שִׁיבָבְתָא בִּישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's wife on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: a wicked neighbor tries to expose the poor wife's empty oven, and the wife hides in shame.

steps.title: The miracle: the oven is full of bread
steps.stepSummary: A miracle happens. The neighbor sees the oven full of bread and the bowl full of dough. She calls out for the wife to bring a shovel before the bread burns. The wife answers that she went inside for exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: A miracle happened for her: the neighbor saw the oven full of bread and the kneading bowl full of dough. She called to her: 'So-and-so, so-and-so! Bring a shovel, your bread is burning!' She answered: 'I too went in for that.'
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven performs a נס to save the wife from shame. The oven really is full of bread, and the wife calmly replies that she went to get a shovel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor came to prove the family had nothing, and instead she saw more bread than expected. The wife's answer, 'I went in for that,' raises a question: was she just covering herself, or did she really go for a shovel? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: A baker's shovel (for taking bread out of the oven)
So-and-so (a woman); stands in for her name

phrases.english: A miracle was done for her,
so that she (the neighbor) saw the oven full of bread
and the kneading bowl full of dough.
She said to her: So-and-so, so-and-so!
Bring a shovel, because your bread is burning!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לָהּ: אַף אֲנָא לְהָכִי עֲיַילִי.
phrases.english: She said to her: I too went in for that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְעֲבִיד לַהּ נִסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension from step 1: the shame is avoided by a miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miracle fills the empty oven with bread, saving the righteous wife from embarrassment.

steps.title: A ברייתא: she really went for a shovel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that the wife was telling the truth. She really went in to get a shovel, because she was used to miracles and expected one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: She too had gone in to bring a shovel, because she was used to miracles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a תנא to explain the wife's answer from step 2. Her words were not an excuse; she really expected a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this line, we might think she only said 'I went in for that' to save face. The ברייתא tells us she truly believed a miracle would come, because miracles happened to her often. This shows her deep trust in ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים)

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a story about being saved from shame into a story about real faith. The wife acted on her trust in ה׳ before she saw the miracle.

phrases.english: It was taught: She too
had gone in to bring a shovel,
because she was used to miracles.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אַף הִיא לְהָבִיא מַרְדֶּה נִכְנְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wife's reply in step 2, showing it was sincere and not an excuse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife truly went for a shovel, because she was accustomed to miracles.

steps.title: The wife asks for help; a golden table leg comes from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: A new episode begins. The wife asks how long they must keep suffering. She tells רבי חנינא בן דוסא to pray for something. He prays, and something like a hand comes out and gives him a leg of a golden table.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife said to him: 'Until when will we keep suffering so much?' He said: 'What can we do?' She said: 'Pray for mercy that they give you something.' He prayed, and something like the palm of a hand came out and gave him one leg of a golden table.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story starts. Because of their poverty, the wife asks her husband to pray for wealth, and Heaven sends him a golden table leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the miracle is not saving them from a moment of shame. It actually makes them rich. The gift seems like a clear answer to the prayer, but the next step shows a hidden cost.

keyTerms.meaning: A leg of a golden table

phrases.english: His wife said to him:

phrases.aramaic: עַד אֵימַת נֵיזִיל וְנִצְטַעַר כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: Until when will we go on suffering so much?
He said to her: What can we do?
(She said:) Pray for mercy that they give you something.
He prayed for mercy,
and something like the palm of a hand came out

phrases.aramaic: וִיהַבוּ לֵיהּ חַד כַּרְעָא דְּפָתוּרָא דְּדַהֲבָא.
phrases.english: and they gave him one leg of a golden table.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ: עַד אֵימַת נֵיזִיל וְנִצְטַעַר כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new episode in the series of stories about רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In answer to prayer, Heaven gives רבי חנינא בן דוסא a leg of a golden table.

steps.title: The dream: their table in the next world will be missing a leg
steps.stepSummary: The wife has a dream. In the future, the צדיקים will eat at golden tables with three legs, but רבי חנינא בן דוסא will eat at a table with only two legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: She saw in a dream that in the future the righteous will eat at a golden table with three legs, but he will eat at a table with two legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The dream shows the hidden cost of the gift. The golden leg was taken from their reward in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leg they got in this world is missing from their table in the next world. So the gift was really an advance payment from their reward for later. This sets up the decision in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future, the righteous will (refers to עולם הבא)

steps.confusionAlert: The table in the dream is not a real piece of furniture. It is a picture of the reward of the צדיקים in עולם הבא. The 'missing leg' means part of their reward was used up.

phrases.english: She saw in a dream
that in the future the righteous will eat at a golden table
that has three legs,
but he will eat at a table with two legs.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזְיָא בְּחֶלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the gift in step 4 came out of their reward in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The golden leg received in this world means their table in עולם הבא will be missing a leg.

steps.title: They pray for the golden leg to be taken back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא asks his wife if she is happy to have a lacking table in the next world. She tells him to pray for the leg to be taken away. He prays, and it is taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: 'Are you content that everyone will eat at a complete table and we at a lacking table?' She said: 'So what can we do? Pray for mercy that they take it from you.' He prayed, and they took it.
steps.whatsHappening: The couple chooses their eternal reward over wealth now. He prays again, and the golden leg is taken back to Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They would rather stay poor in this world than lose any part of their reward in עולם הבא. The same way he prayed to receive, he now prays to give it back. The prayer is answered, which the next step calls an even bigger miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it acceptable to you? Are you content?

phrases.english: He said to her: Are you content

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵיכָל אָכְלִי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אַפָּתוּרָא דְּמַשְׁלַם
phrases.english: that everyone will eat at a complete table
and we at a lacking table?
She said to him: So what can we do?
Pray for mercy that they take it from you.
He prayed for mercy, and they took it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: נִיחָא לָךְ דְּמֵיכָל אָכְלִי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אַפָּתוּרָא דְּמַשְׁלַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the dream in step 5 by reversing the gift from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They prefer their full reward in עולם הבא, so they pray and the golden leg is taken back.

steps.title: The second miracle was greater than the first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the miracle of taking the leg back was greater than the miracle of giving it. There is a tradition that Heaven gives gifts but does not take them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The last miracle was greater than the first. For we have a tradition that Heaven gives, but does not take back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story with a ברייתא that judges the two miracles. Taking the leg back was the bigger miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once Heaven gives a gift, it stays given. Taking it back broke that normal rule, so it needed a bigger miracle than the first gift. This shows how great רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayers were.

keyTerms.meaning: For we have a tradition (literally, 'we learned')
They (Heaven) give, but they do not take back

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן דוסא and his wife chose to stay poor rather than use up their reward in עולם הבא. The return of the golden leg was a greater miracle than receiving it, because Heaven does not usually take back what it gives.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general rule found in the גמרא: a gift from Heaven is not normally taken back. It also teaches a value: eternal reward is worth more than comfort in this world.

phrases.english: It was taught: The last miracle was greater
than the first.
For we have a tradition
that they (Heaven) give, but do not take back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: גָּדוֹל הָיָה נֵס אַחֲרוֹן יוֹתֵר מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the two miracles from steps 4 and 6 and closes the episode.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Taking the golden leg back was a greater miracle than giving it, because Heaven's gifts are normally never taken back.

steps.title: The daughter lights the שבת lamp with vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's daughter is sad because she lit the שבת lamp with vinegar instead of oil. He tells her that the One Who made oil burn can make vinegar burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ערב שבת, he saw that his daughter was sad. He said to her: My daughter, why are you sad? She said to him: I mixed up a jug of vinegar with a jug of oil, and I lit the שבת light with it. He said to her: My daughter, why should this bother you? The One Who told oil to burn can tell vinegar to burn.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins about רבי חנינא בן דוסא. His daughter is upset about a mistake with the שבת lamp, and he calms her with words of complete trust in ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar does not normally burn, so she expected the house to go dark on שבת. רבי חנינא בן דוסא teaches that oil burns only because ה׳ commands it, so vinegar can burn just as easily if ה׳ wants. This matches what we saw in the earlier stories: his family lived with miracles as a normal part of life.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight; here it means the start of שבת, Friday evening
Why should it bother you? / What do you care?

steps.whyThisMatters: This line sums up רבי חנינא בן דוסא's whole outlook. Nature itself is only ה׳'s command, so a miracle is not harder for Him than nature.

phrases.english: One Shabbat evening (at twilight),
phrases.notes: The subject is רבי חנינא בן דוסא, continuing from the earlier stories.

phrases.english: he saw that his daughter was sad.
He said to her: My daughter, why are you sad?
She said to him: A jug of vinegar
got mixed up for me with a jug of oil,
and I lit the Shabbat light with it.
phrases.notes: She is afraid that the lamp will soon go out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: בִּתִּי, מַאי אִכְפַּת לִךְ?
phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter, why should this bother you?
The One Who told the oil to burn
can tell the vinegar to burn.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי חַזְיַיהּ לְבַרְתֵּיהּ דַּהֲווֹת עֲצִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new episode in the chain of רבי חנינא בן דוסא miracle stories, after the golden table story ended in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The power of anything to burn comes from ה׳'s word, so vinegar can burn as well as oil.

steps.title: The vinegar lamp burns until הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that the vinegar lamp burned all of שבת. They even used its flame for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: It kept on burning the whole day, until they took fire from it for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא finishes the story and tells us what happened. The vinegar really did burn, and it lasted for all of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story itself only told us what רבי חנינא בן דוסא said. The ברייתא adds the result: his words came true. The miracle was even bigger than needed, because the lamp lasted long enough to light the הבדלה candle.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא taught; this introduces a ברייתא
The ceremony at the end of שבת

phrases.english: A תנא taught: It kept on burning
the entire day,
until they brought fire from it for הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הָיָה דּוֹלֵק וְהוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the vinegar story with its miraculous outcome, as reported in a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vinegar lamp burned all שבת and supplied the flame for הבדלה.

steps.title: Neighbors complain about his goats
steps.stepSummary: People complain that רבי חנינא בן דוסא's goats are causing damage. He declares: if it is true, let bears eat them; if not, let each goat bring home a bear on its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן דוסא had some goats. People said to him: They are causing damage. He said: If they are causing damage, let bears eat them. But if not, let each one of them bring a bear on its horns this evening.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבי חנינא בן דוסא answers an accusation against his goats by setting up a test that only Heaven can decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with the neighbors. Instead, he leaves the judgment to ה׳. If the goats are guilty, they should be punished by bears. If they are innocent, they should prove it in a way nobody could deny. This step only sets up the test; the result comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ הָנָךְ עִיזֵּי,
phrases.english: רבי חנינא בן דוסא had some goats.
They said to him: They are causing damage.
phrases.notes: The goats were said to be eating in other people's fields.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: אִי קָא מַפְסְדָן — נֵיכְלִינְהוּ דּוּבֵּי,
phrases.english: He said: If they are causing damage, let bears eat them.
But if not, let each and every one
bring a bear on its horns this evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ הָנָךְ עִיזֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate miracle story about רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא sets up a test for Heaven to decide: bears will either punish the goats or be carried home by them.

steps.title: Each goat comes home with a bear
steps.stepSummary: That evening, every goat came back carrying a bear on its horns, which proved that the goats were innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the evening, each and every one brought a bear on its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the result of the test from the step before. The goats are proven innocent in an amazing way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording repeats his words almost exactly. This shows that what he said happened exactly as he said it. The accusation was false, and Heaven proved it.

phrases.english: In the evening, each and every one brought
a bear on its horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאוּרְתָּא אַיְיתַי כֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of the test set up in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The goats were innocent, and Heaven proved it exactly the way רבי חנינא בן דוסא had said.

steps.title: The neighbor's beams are too short, and he blesses them
steps.stepSummary: A neighbor building a house finds that her beams are too short. רבי חנינא בן דוסא asks her name, and when she says 'איכו,' he blesses her beams to reach the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a certain neighbor who was building a house, and the beams did not reach. She came before him and said: I built my house, and my beams do not reach. He said to her: What is your name? She said to him: איכו. He said: איכו (if so), may your beams reach.
steps.whatsHappening: Another new story begins. A neighbor's ceiling beams are too short to reach from wall to wall, and רבי חנינא בן דוסא blesses them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beams were not long enough to rest on both walls, so the roof could not be built. He asks her name and turns it into a blessing. 'איכו' sounds like a word meaning 'if so' (אי הכי), so he says: if so, may your beams reach. The step tells us the blessing; the next steps show how it came true.

keyTerms.meaning: The neighbor's name, which sounds like 'if so'

phrases.english: He had a certain neighbor
who was building a house,
and the beams did not reach from wall to wall.
She came before him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: בְּנֵיתִי בֵּיתִי וְלָא קָמָטוּ כְּשׁוּרַאי.
phrases.english: and said to him: I built my house, but my beams do not reach.
He said to her: What is your name?
She said to him: Ikku.
He said: If so (Ikku), may your beams reach.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא שִׁיבָבְתָא דְּקָא בָנְיָא בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate miracle story about רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא blesses the short beams so that they will reach the walls.

steps.title: How far the beams grew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the beams grew so much that they stuck out a cubit on each side. Another opinion says they were extended with added pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: They reached so far that they stuck out a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side. And some say: they were made with added extensions.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא describes the result of the blessing. Two versions are given of how the beams came to reach the walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the beams themselves grew longer, so long that they stuck out past both walls. The 'some say' opinion describes it differently: extensions (סניפין) were what made them reach. Either way, the blessing worked.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side
And some say; this introduces another opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The 'some say' opinion is not denying the miracle. It only gives a different picture of how the beams came to reach the walls.

phrases.english: A תנא taught: They reached so far that they stuck out
a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side.
And some say: they were made with extensions.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הִגִּיעוּ עַד שֶׁיָּצְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the outcome of the blessing from step 12, with two versions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams grew past the walls by a cubit on each side; another opinion says extensions made them reach.

steps.title: פלימו saw the house with his own eyes
steps.stepSummary: The sage פלימו testifies that he saw the house. Its beams stuck out a cubit on each side, and people told him it was the house that רבי חנינא בן דוסא roofed through his prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: פלימו says: I saw that house, and its beams stuck out a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side. And they told me: This is the house that רבי חנינא בן דוסא roofed through his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings eyewitness support for the story. פלימו personally saw the beams sticking out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This testimony matches the first version in the step before: the beams stuck out a cubit on each side. It shows that the story was known in later times, and the house could still be seen. It also calls the blessing a תפילה, which shows that his miracles came through prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A תנא who gives eyewitness testimony

steps.whatToRemember: These stories (the vinegar lamp, the goats, the beams) all show the same idea: for רבי חנינא בן דוסא‎, ה׳ changed nature in response to his trust and his prayer.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: פלימו says:
I saw that house,
and its beams stuck out
a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side,
and they said to me: This is the house

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁקֵּירָה רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ.
phrases.english: that רבי חנינא בן דוסא roofed through his prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, פְּלֵימוֹ אוֹמֵר: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אוֹתוֹ הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first version in step 13 (beams sticking out a cubit on each side) with eyewitness testimony.
steps.raayaObject: That the beams miraculously grew and stuck out a cubit on each side
steps.raayaSupportSource: The eyewitness testimony of פלימו in a ברייתא

steps.title: How could a poor man own goats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges a detail of the goat story: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was poor, and raising small animals in ארץ ישראל is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did רבי חנינא בן דוסא get goats from? He was poor! Also, the חכמים said you may not raise small animals in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and questions the earlier goat story. It gives two problems: he was too poor to own goats, and owning goats is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first problem is practical: a very poor man could not afford a herd. The second problem is legal: the חכמים banned raising sheep and goats in ארץ ישראל because they graze in other people's fields. Both problems make the earlier story hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Small animals, such as sheep and goats

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa
from where did he have goats?
But he was poor!
phrases.notes: Refers back to the earlier stories about his poverty.

phrases.english: And furthermore, the Sages said:
One may not raise small animals
phrases.notes: They graze in and damage other people's fields.

phrases.english: in Eretz Yisrael?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא מֵהֵיכָן הֲווֹ לֵיהּ עִזִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a detail of the goat story told in steps 10-11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חנינא בן דוסא owned goats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He was poor, so he could not afford goats. Also, raising small animals in ארץ ישראל is forbidden, so a צדיק would not keep them.

steps.title: רב פנחס explains: lost chickens turned into goats
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס tells a story. A man left chickens at רבי חנינא's door, and רבי חנינא refused to eat their eggs. When the chickens multiplied, he sold them and bought goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס said: A man once left chickens at the door of רבי חנינא's house, and his wife found them. He told her not to eat their eggs. The eggs and chickens multiplied and bothered them, so he sold them and bought goats with the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פנחס answers the question by explaining how the goats came to be there. They were never bought with רבי חנינא's own money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goats came from someone else's lost chickens, so his poverty is no longer a problem. רבי חנינא treated the chickens as a lost object (אבידה) belonging to their owner and would not even eat the eggs. When caring for the chickens became too hard, he turned them into goats, which were easier to look after, while still holding the value for the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: With their money (the money from selling them)

steps.confusionAlert: The goats were not really רבי חנינא's own animals. He was only watching over the value of someone else's lost chickens. That is why this does not prove he was rich.

phrases.english: Rav Pinchas said:
There was an incident: a certain man passed by
the entrance of his (Rabbi Chanina's) house
and left chickens there,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְצָאָתַן אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא,
phrases.english: and the wife of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa found them,
and he said to her:
Do not eat from their eggs.
And the eggs and chickens multiplied
and they were bothering them,
so he sold them and bought goats with their money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פִּנְחָס: מַעֲשֶׂה וְעָבַר אָדָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by explaining where the goats came from.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא owned goats, which seems impossible for a poor man and forbidden by law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The goats came from someone else's lost chickens that רבי חנינא was guarding. He did not buy them with his own money.

steps.title: The owner returns and receives the goats
steps.stepSummary: The man who lost the chickens passes by. He proves his ownership with a סימן and takes the goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, the man who lost the chickens passed by and told his friend, 'Here is where I left my chickens.' רבי חנינא heard and asked, 'Do you have a sign to identify them?' He said yes, gave the sign, and took the goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues, and the lost property goes back to its owner. This shows the goats were never really רבי חנינא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא follows the halacha of returning lost objects: the owner must give a סימן, an identifying sign. Once he does, he receives the goats bought with his chickens' value. This shows the goats were never רבי חנינא's own property, which answers how a poor man could have goats.

keyTerms.meaning: An identifying sign that proves ownership of a lost object

phrases.english: Once, that same man passed by
who had lost the chickens
and said to his friend:
Here is where I left my chickens.
Rabbi Chanina heard, and said to him:
Do you have a sign to identify them?
He said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לוֹ סִימָן וְנָטַל אֶת הָעִיזִּין,
phrases.english: He gave him the sign and took the goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת עָבַר אוֹתוֹ אָדָם שֶׁאָבְדוּ מִמֶּנּוּ הַתַּרְנְגוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב פנחס's story and finishes the answer to step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goats were returned to the true owner after he gave a סימן.

steps.title: These were the goats that brought the bears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ties the story together: these were the same goats that came home carrying bears on their horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these were the very goats that brought bears on their horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects רב פנחס's story back to the miracle of the bears from step 11. This closes the discussion about the goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goats that came home with bears on their horns are identified as the goats bought from the lost chickens. This answers how the poor רבי חנינא had goats at all. It also fits his character: he guarded someone else's property honestly, and Heaven protected that property.

keyTerms.meaning: And these are the very same

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's goats were really someone else's lost chickens, turned into goats and later returned to the owner. Bought with no money of his own, they are the same goats that came home carrying bears.

phrases.english: And these are the very goats
that brought bears on their horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵן הֵן עִיזֵּי דְּאַיְיתוֹ דּוּבֵּי בְּקַרְנַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רב פנחס's story back to the bear miracle and closes the question of step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The miracle goats were the goats bought from the lost chickens, so this does not show רבי חנינא was wealthy.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן פדת's poverty and strange sleep
steps.stepSummary: A new story: the very poor רבי אלעזר בן פדת has bloodletting done and has nothing to eat afterward but garlic. He falls asleep, and the חכמים see him crying, laughing, and glowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן פדת was very poor. He had bloodletting done and had nothing to eat afterward. He took a clove of garlic and put it in his mouth, grew faint, and fell asleep. The חכמים came to visit him and saw him crying and laughing, with a ray of light coming from his forehead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about another poor צדיק. This step sets the scene for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After bloodletting a person must eat something, but he had only a piece of garlic, so he became weak and dozed off. While he slept, the visiting חכמים saw three strange things: crying, laughing, and a light shining from his face. These details make us want to know what he was dreaming.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask about his welfare (to visit him)
A ray of fire or light

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat
was very hard-pressed (for money).
He had 'a thing' done (bloodletting)
phrases.notes: A polite way of referring to bloodletting.

phrases.english: and he did not have anything to taste afterward,
so he took a clove of garlic
and put it in his mouth.
His heart grew weak and he dozed off.
The Rabbis went to ask about his welfare,
and they saw him crying and laughing,
and a ray of fire came out from his forehead.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פְּדָת דְּחִיקָא לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story in the series about poor צדיקים, after finishing the stories of רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן פדת was so poor that he had only garlic after bloodletting. In his sleep he was seen crying, laughing, and glowing.

steps.title: The Sages ask why he cried and laughed
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אלעזר wakes up, the חכמים ask him why he was crying and laughing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he woke up, they asked him: Why were you crying and laughing?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask a simple question about the strange things they saw. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crying and laughing at the same time point to something both painful and joyful. This question opens the door to his dream.

phrases.english: When he woke up, they said to him:
Why were you crying and laughing?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִתְּעַר, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קָבָכֵית וְחָיְיכַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the strange behavior described in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason he was crying and laughing in his sleep

steps.title: His dream: a conversation with ה׳ about his suffering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the הקדוש ברוך הוא sat with him in his dream. He asked how long he must suffer. ה׳ answered: should I restart the whole world so that you might be born at a time of livelihood?
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them: The הקדוש ברוך הוא was sitting with me, and I asked Him, 'Until when will I suffer in this world?' He answered me, 'אלעזר, My son, would you like Me to turn the world back to its beginning? Maybe you will be born at a time of livelihood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר begins to explain his dream. The conversation continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His poverty is tied to the time he was born. Changing it would mean starting the whole world over. Even then, ה׳ says only 'perhaps' (אפשר) he would be born at a better time, which shows how hard such a change would be.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
An hour (time) of livelihood or sustenance

steps.confusionAlert: ה׳'s words are a question, not a promise. ה׳ is not offering to rebuild the world. He is showing how deep the problem goes, and even then success is only 'perhaps.'

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב עִמִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, was sitting with me,
and I said to Him:
Until when will I suffer in this world?
And He said to me: Elazar, My son,
would you like Me to turn the world back to its beginning?
Perhaps you will be born at a time of livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב עִמִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' question from step 20 by describing the dream.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was crying and laughing because of a dream in which he spoke with the הקדוש ברוך הוא about his suffering. ה׳ said that changing his poverty would mean restarting the world, and even that might not help.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows that a person's livelihood is tied to his מזל, the time he was born. That idea goes on to shape the rest of this conversation in the גמרא.

steps.title: All that, and still only a maybe?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks: even if the whole world were restarted, would it only possibly turn out better?
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before Him: All this trouble, and it is only a possibility?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר reacts to ה׳'s offer to restart the world. He asks whether such a huge step would still only maybe change his fate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 ה׳ said that restarting the world might let him be born at a better time. רבי אלעזר notices the word 'maybe.' Restarting everything would not guarantee him a good livelihood.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is only possible / maybe

phrases.english: I said before Him:
All this, and it is only a possibility?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרִי לְקַמֵּיהּ: כּוּלֵּי הַאי, וְאֶפְשָׁר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to ה׳'s offer in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether restarting the world would even guarantee a better result

steps.title: Have I lived more, or will I live more?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether most of his life is already behind him or still ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to Him: Is the part I have already lived longer, or the part I still will live?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks a second question. He wants to know how much of his life is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is weighing whether a restart is worth it. If most of his life is already over, there is little gain in restarting everything for a few remaining years.

phrases.english: I said to Him:
Is what I have lived more, or what I will live?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרִי לֵיהּ: דַּחֲיַי טְפֵי אוֹ דְחָיֵינָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question to judge whether the restart is worth it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether more of his life is in the past or the future

steps.title: You have already lived most of it
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers that most of his life has already passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: The part you have already lived is longer.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers the question from step 23. Most of רבי אלעזר's years are already behind him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer settles his calculation. Only a small part of his life remains.

phrases.english: He said to me: What you have lived.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: דַּחֲיֵית.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: More of his life has already passed than remains

steps.title: Then I do not want it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר turns down the offer to restart the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before Him: If so, I do not want it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר draws his conclusion. It is not worth restarting the world for so few years, so he declines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the exchange from step 21. He accepts his hard life instead of asking for a huge change that might not even help.

phrases.english: I said before Him:
If so, I do not want it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרִי לְקַמֵּיהּ: אִם כֵּן, לָא בָּעֵינָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes based on the answer in step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר declines a restart of the world and accepts his lot

steps.title: The reward: thirteen rivers of balsam oil
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ rewards רבי אלעזר in עולם הבא with thirteen huge rivers of pure balsam oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: As a reward for saying 'I do not want,' I will give you in עולם הבא thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil, as big as the Euphrates and the Tigris, for you to enjoy.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ rewards רבי אלעזר for accepting his situation. He promises him great pleasure in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His refusal is treated as a meritorious act that earns reward. The poor man who had only garlic to eat is promised enormous riches in the next world.

phrases.english: He said to me:
As a reward for saying 'I do not want'
I will give you in the World to Come
thirteen rivers of balsam oil
pure, as big as the Euphrates and the Tigris,
that you will enjoy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: בְּהַאי אַגְרָא דַּאֲמַרְתְּ ״לָא בָּעֵינָא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ה׳ responds to his refusal with a reward
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting one's lot earns great reward in עולם הבא

steps.title: Only this and nothing more?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether that is the whole reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before Him: This, and no more?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר boldly asks whether he will get anything beyond the thirteen rivers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a warm, close conversation, not ingratitude. The question sets up ה׳'s reply about the other צדיקים.

phrases.english: I said before Him:
This, and no more?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרִי לְקַמֵּיהּ: הַאי וְתוּ לָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reward given in step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is more reward beyond the rivers

steps.title: What would be left for your friends?
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers that if He gave more, there would be nothing to give his colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: And what will I give your friends?
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ replies with a question of His own. If רבי אלעזר gets more, what will be left for the other צדיקים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reply is worded as a question, but it works as an answer. It explains why the reward is limited: other people also need to be rewarded.

phrases.english: He said to me:
And to your friends, what will I give?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לִי: וּלְחַבְרָךְ מַאי יָהֵיבְנָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 with a question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reward is limited so that others can also receive theirs

steps.title: Am I asking from someone who doesn't have enough?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר pushes back: ה׳ has no limit, so giving him more takes nothing from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to Him: And am I asking from a person who does not have enough?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges ה׳'s answer. ה׳ is not a man with limited supplies, so He can give everyone without running out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 28 assumes a limited amount to share. רבי אלעזר answers that this does not apply to ה׳, who is all-powerful.

phrases.english: I said to Him:
And am I asking from a man who doesn't have?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרִי לֵיהּ: וַאֲנָא מִגַּבְרָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ בָּעֵינָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: ה׳'s reason in step 28 that there must be something left for others
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shortage only applies to a human giver. ה׳'s supply is unlimited.

steps.title: A flick on the forehead: why he was glowing
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ playfully flicks רבי אלעזר's forehead and calls him 'my son,' which explains the glow the חכמים saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: He flicked His finger on my forehead and said to me: אלעזר, my son, I shoot My arrows at you.
steps.whatsHappening: The dream ends with an affectionate flick on the forehead. This answers the last mystery from step 19: why רבי אלעזר's face was glowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the חכמים saw him crying, laughing, and glowing. He cried over his suffering, laughed at the promised reward, and glowed from ה׳'s touch on his forehead. The words 'My arrows' express loving playfulness, not anger.
steps.whatToRemember: The dream explains all three things the חכמים saw: crying over his poverty, laughing at his reward, and glowing from ה׳'s loving touch.
steps.confusionAlert: 'I shoot My arrows at you' is not a punishment here. It describes a loving, playful gesture, and that touch is what made his face shine.

phrases.english: He flicked with His finger on my forehead,
and said to me:
Elazar, my son, I shoot My arrows at you.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְיַין בְּאִסְקוּטְלָא אַפּוּתַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the dream and closes the story begun in step 19
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳'s affectionate touch explains the glow on רבי אלעזר's face

steps.title: רבי חמא בר חנינא's fast brings no rain
steps.stepSummary: A new story: רבי חמא בר חנינא decrees a fast, but no rain falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא decreed a fast, and rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, fasting for rain, and begins a new story. A fast was decreed but did not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the problem the story will deal with. Why did this fast fail when others succeeded?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina decreed a fast
and rain did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, returning to the topic of fasting for rain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast decreed by רבי חמא בר חנינא did not bring rain

steps.title: But רבי יהושע בן לוי's fast did bring rain!
steps.stepSummary: The people point out that when רבי יהושע בן לוי fasted, rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But רבי יהושע בן לוי decreed a fast, and rain came!
steps.whatsHappening: The people challenge רבי חמא. Another sage, רבי יהושע בן לוי, decreed a fast and it worked, so why didn't his?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that a fast should bring rain for anyone who does it properly. רבי יהושע בן לוי's success makes רבי חמא's failure look strange.

keyTerms.meaning: A great sage whose fast brought rain

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי גָּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi decreed a fast
and rain came!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי גָּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the failure described in step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: The failure of רבי חמא's fast
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהושע בן לוי's fast brought rain, the same should happen for רבי חמא

steps.title: He is greater than I am
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא humbly answers that he is not on the level of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is me, and that is the son of Levi.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא answers the challenge. He and רבי יהושע בן לוי are not equals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer explains the difference by the person, not the fast. A greater צדיק's prayer is answered more easily, and רבי חמא humbly puts himself on a lower level.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of Levi (רבי יהושע בן לוי)

phrases.english: He said to them:
This is me, and that is the son of Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָא אֲנָא, הָא בַּר לֵיוַאי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any properly decreed fast should bring rain equally
steps.terutzMaskana: Success depends on the stature of the one leading the fast

steps.title: Let us pray with real focus
steps.stepSummary: The people suggest praying with full concentration, hoping the community's hearts will break and bring rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Let us come and focus our minds. Maybe the community's hearts will break, and rain will come.
steps.whatsHappening: The people propose a new plan. If everyone prays with a broken, sincere heart, maybe the rain will come even without a great leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This suggests a different way to earn rain: the sincerity of the whole community instead of the stature of one leader. It sets up the test in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: That their hearts will break (become humble)

phrases.english: They said to him: Let us come and focus our minds,
perhaps the community will break their hearts
and rain will come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: דְּנֵיתֵי וְנִיכַוֵּין דַּעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another path after רבי חמא says he lacks the stature
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A community's heartfelt prayer might bring rain

steps.title: They prayed, but still no rain
steps.stepSummary: The community prays for mercy, but rain still does not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: They prayed for mercy, and rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The plan from step 34 is tried and fails. Even focused prayer brings no rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The result knocks down the community's suggestion. It sets up the final approach that רבי חמא will use.

phrases.english: They prayed for mercy, and rain did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹן רַחֲמֵי וְלָא אָתֵי מִיטְרָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the plan in step 34 did not work
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The community's focused prayer did not bring rain in practice

steps.title: Do you agree to rain coming in our merit?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא asks the people if they are content for rain to come on his account.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Is it fine with you that rain should come because of us?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא asks the people for permission. Are they willing for the rain to come through his own merit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier he humbly refused to compare himself to רבי יהושע בן לוי. Now, since nothing else has worked, he asks their consent before acting on his own merit. This sets up his next action.

keyTerms.meaning: On our account / in our merit

phrases.english: He said to them:
Are you content that rain should come on our account?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: נִיחָא לְכוּ שֶׁיָּבֹא מָטָר בִּשְׁבִילֵנוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the community's prayer fails, רבי חמא offers his own approach
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the people agree to rain coming through his merit

steps.title: Yes
steps.stepSummary: The people agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The people give their consent. This clears the way for רבי חמא's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their agreement matters because רבי חמא would not act on his own merit without their consent.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הֵן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 36

steps.title: Sky, cover your face!
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא commands the sky to cover itself with clouds, but at first nothing happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Sky, sky, cover your face! It did not become covered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא speaks directly to the sky and orders it to fill with clouds. At first the sky does not respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is his first attempt at bringing rain through his own merit. The failure creates suspense for the final step.

phrases.english: He said: Sky, sky, cover your face!
It did not become covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: רָקִיעַ רָקִיעַ כַּסֵּי פָּנֶיךָ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acts on the consent given in step 37
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חמא commands the sky, but it does not obey at first

steps.title: How brazen is the sky! Then the rain came
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא rebukes the sky for ignoring him. It becomes covered with clouds and the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: How impudent is the face of the sky! It became covered, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא scolds the sky for not listening. Right away it fills with clouds and the rain falls, ending the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who called himself less than רבי יהושע בן לוי turns out to have real power once he acts in his own merit. The story ends with the rain they had been seeking from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חמא בר חנינא's fast first failed and the community's prayer failed too, but when he acted in his own merit and rebuked the sky, the rain came.

phrases.english: He said: How impudent is the face of the sky,
it became covered, and rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: כַּמָּה עַזִּין פְּנֵי רָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the attempt from step 38 and resolves the story begun in step 31
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through רבי חמא's merit and rebuke of the sky, the rain finally came

steps.title: לוי's fast fails and he speaks harshly to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: לוי declares a fast and no rain comes. He complains to ה׳ that He sits on high and has no mercy on His children.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי decreed a fast, and rain did not come. He said before ה׳: רבונו של עולם! You went up and sat on high, and You do not have mercy on Your children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new rain story. When לוי's fast does not bring rain, he speaks to ה׳ in a sharp, complaining way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier stories, the fast fails at first. Here, though, לוי's words are not a gentle request. They accuse ה׳ of being distant and uncaring, and this sets up the result in the next step.

phrases.english: Levi decreed a fast
and rain did not come.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
You went up and sat on high
and You do not have mercy on Your children.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא וְלָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rain story that follows רבי חמא's story, where he spoke boldly to the sky.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי's fast fails, and he speaks harshly toward ה׳.

steps.title: The rain comes, but לוי becomes lame
steps.stepSummary: Rain falls, but לוי is punished by becoming lame.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rain came, and he became lame.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with two results. The rain comes, but לוי becomes lame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His prayer was answered, so the bold words worked. Even so, he paid a personal price for speaking harshly toward Heaven.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rain failed. The rain did come. The lameness was a separate punishment for how לוי spoke.

phrases.english: Rain came,
and he became lame.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא מִיטְרָא, וְאִיטְּלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of לוי's harsh words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Bold words can bring results, but speaking harshly toward Heaven carries a cost.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's warning: never speak harshly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from this story that a person should never speak harshly toward ה׳, because לוי did and became lame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A person should never speak harsh words toward Heaven. After all, a great man spoke harsh words toward Heaven and became lame. And who was he? לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר turns the story into a general lesson. Do not speak harshly toward Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is stronger because it involves an אדם גדול. If even a great person was punished, an ordinary person should surely be careful.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a lasting rule of proper speech toward ה׳, even when someone is in distress.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יָטִיחַ אָדָם דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה,
phrases.english: A person should never cast harsh words toward Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אָדָם גָּדוֹל הֵטִיחַ דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
phrases.english: for a great man cast harsh words toward Heaven
and became lame,
and who was he? Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לְעוֹלָם אַל יָטִיחַ אָדָם דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from לוי's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should never speak harshly toward Heaven.

steps.title: Was לוי not lamed by performing קידה before רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that his words caused the lameness. Another source says לוי became lame from showing קידה before רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did this cause his lameness? But לוי demonstrated קידה (a special bow) before רבי and became lame!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a conflict with another story. That story gives a different cause for לוי's lameness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere (מגילה 22b) we learn that לוי was injured while demonstrating קידה, a difficult bow face-down. If that physical act caused the injury, how can רבי אלעזר say his words did?

keyTerms.meaning: a special bow with the face to the ground

phrases.english: Did this cause it for him?
But Levi demonstrated kidda
before Rabbi, and became lame!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גְּרַמָא לֵיהּ? וְהָא לֵוִי אַחְוִי קִידָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's explanation of the cause.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that harsh words caused לוי's lameness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another tradition gives a different cause, the injury from performing קידה.

steps.title: Both causes together made him lame
steps.stepSummary: Both the harsh words and the קידה caused the lameness.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that caused it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two stories do not conflict. Both factors worked together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harsh words made לוי deserve a punishment. The punishment came in the form of an injury during the difficult bow.
steps.whatToRemember: לוי's lameness came from both his harsh words (the reason) and the קידה (the way it happened).

phrases.english: This and that caused it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא וְהָא גְּרַמָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one cause could explain the lameness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words were the spiritual cause, and the קידה was the physical way it happened.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר לוליני hears clouds heading to עמון and מואב
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר לוליני hears clouds planning to bring rain to עמון and מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר לוליני heard these clouds saying: Let us go and pour water on עמון and מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rain story begins. It sets up רבי חייא בר לוליני's argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clouds are about to bring rain to other nations instead of to ישראל. This creates the problem he will argue against.

keyTerms.meaning: Ammon and Moab, nations east of the Jordan

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Lulyani
heard these clouds saying:
Let us go and pour water on Ammon and Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר לוּלְיָינִי שַׁמְעִינְהוּ לְהָנָךְ עֲנָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rain story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clouds plan to rain on עמון and מואב.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר לוליני argues that the nations who rejected the תורה should not get rain
steps.stepSummary: He argues to ה׳ that the nations refused the תורה, so they should not receive rain. He tells the clouds to pour it here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before ה׳: רבונו של עולם! When You gave the תורה to Your nation ישראל, You went around to all the nations of the world and they did not accept it. And now You are giving them rain? Pour it here!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר לוליני challenges the plan to give rain to the nations. Then he directs the rain to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is that the nations turned down the תורה, while ישראל accepted it. So ישראל deserves the rain more. Unlike לוי, he argues respectfully for his people instead of accusing ה׳.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
When You gave the Torah to Your nation Israel,
You went around to all the nations of the world
and they did not accept it,
and now You are giving them rain?
Pour it here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! כְּשֶׁנָּתַתָּ תּוֹרָה לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the clouds' plan.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to give rain to עמון and מואב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nations that refused the תורה should not receive the rain that ישראל needs.

steps.title: The clouds pour the rain in their place
steps.stepSummary: The clouds pour their rain in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They poured it in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with success. The rain falls in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His respectful argument works with no punishment. This is the opposite of what happened to לוי.
steps.whatToRemember: לוי accused ה׳ and was punished. רבי חייא בר לוליני argued for ישראל's merit and succeeded.

phrases.english: They poured it in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁדְיוּהּ אַדּוּכְתַּיְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of his request.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rain falls in ארץ ישראל because of רבי חייא בר לוליני's argument.

steps.title: Why is a צדיק compared to both a palm tree and a cedar?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר לוליני asks why the פסוק compares a צדיק to both a תמר and an ארז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר לוליני taught: What is the meaning of what is written: "The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon"? If it says palm tree, why does it say cedar, and if it says cedar, why does it say palm tree?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי חייא בר לוליני was just mentioned, the גמרא brings one of his teachings. It begins with a question on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about extra wording. Why use two comparisons when one should be enough? Each tree must teach something the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Lulyani taught,
what is the meaning of what is written:
"The righteous will flourish like a palm tree;
he will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon",

phrases.aramaic: אִם נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז,
phrases.english: if palm tree is said, why is cedar said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר?
phrases.english: and if cedar is said, why is palm tree said?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר לוּלְיָינִי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching from the same רבי, connected by his name.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק needs both comparisons

steps.title: Starting the answer: what we would think from the palm tree alone
steps.stepSummary: He begins answering by showing what we would wrongly think if only the תמר were mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If palm tree were said and cedar were not said, I would have said: just as a palm tree...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא begins the answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a "what would I have thought" method. If only the תמר were mentioned, we would draw a wrong conclusion, so the ארז comes to fix it. The details come next.

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז,
phrases.english: If palm tree were said and cedar were not said,
I would have said: just as a palm tree

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each tree prevents a wrong conclusion we would draw from the other alone. The answer continues on the next amud.
